newsitem.title: USA: End of state school property tax in Kansas bill.
newsitem.headline: End of state school property tax in Kansas bill.

text.p: A Kansas lawmaker has introduced a bill to eliminate a state property tax levy on homeowners that helps fund primary and secondary schools.

State Rep. Phill Kline, R-Shawnee, said Friday his bill would eliminate the residential levy and reduce by 25 percent the commercial property tax levy. He said the $166 million that would be lost under the plan would be replaced by tapping into a state budget surplus, projected to be as high as $300 million.
"There is no reduction in school funding," said Kline, who is chairman of the House Taxation Committee.

Kline's plan already had competition from Gov. Bill Graves, who proposed this week a two-year, 30 percent reduction in the school levy. The state levy is used to equalize per-pupil funding of public schools.
In addition, State Rep. Ed NcKechnie, D-Pittsburg, also introduced a measure aimed at amending the state's constitution to eliminate property taxes.
